inputs.description: EC2 instance ID. Leave empty to resolve the target from the application name.
Application / service name, matched against the EC2 Name tag. Used to resolve the target when no instance ID is given, and to locate the systemd unit on the host.
How far back to look for metrics, alarms and logs (Go duration, e.g. 30m, 1h, 6h).
CloudWatch Logs group holding the application logs. Leave empty to skip the log evidence check.
CloudWatch Logs filter pattern applied to the log group.
Comma-separated host:port list probed from the instance itself (e.g. db.internal:5432,cache.internal:6379). Leave empty to skip connectivity probes.
Run the on-host evidence script over AWS SSM. Requires the SSM agent and an instance profile with AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore.
Incident or event identifier, echoed into the diagnostic result for traceability.
Event to attach the diagnostic result to. Leave empty to run standalone.

params.command: aws ec2 describe-instances --region {{ Inputs.region }} {% if Inputs.instance_id %}--instance-ids {{ Inputs.instance_id }}{% else %}--filters Name=tag:Name,Values="{{ Inputs.application }}"{% endif %} --output json --query "Reservations[].Instances[].{InstanceId:InstanceId,State:State.Name,StateReason:StateTransitionReason,Type:InstanceType,Az:Placement.AvailabilityZone,PrivateIp:PrivateIpAddress,PublicIp:PublicIpAddress,LaunchTime:LaunchTime,Name:Tags[?Key=='Name']|[0].Value}"

aws cloudwatch describe-alarms --region {{ Inputs.region }} --state-value ALARM --max-items 200 --output json --query "MetricAlarms[].{Name:AlarmName,Metric:MetricName,Namespace:Namespace,Reason:StateReason,Updated:StateUpdatedTimestamp,Dimensions:Dimensions}"

aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --region {{ Inputs.region }} --namespace AWS/EC2 --metric-name CPUUtilization --dimensions Name=InstanceId,Value={{ Tasks.select_instance.output.data.instance_id }} --start-time {{ Tasks.time_window.output.data.start_iso }} --end-time {{ Tasks.time_window.output.data.end_iso }} --period 300 --statistics Average Maximum --output json

aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --region {{ Inputs.region }} --namespace AWS/EC2 --metric-name StatusCheckFailed --dimensions Name=InstanceId,Value={{ Tasks.select_instance.output.data.instance_id }} --start-time {{ Tasks.time_window.output.data.start_iso }} --end-time {{ Tasks.time_window.output.data.end_iso }} --period 300 --statistics Maximum Sum --output json

aws elbv2 describe-target-health --region {{ Inputs.region }} --target-group-arn {{ LoopItem.arn }} --output json --query "TargetHealthDescriptions[].{Id:Target.Id,Port:Target.Port,State:TargetHealth.State,Reason:TargetHealth.Reason,Description:TargetHealth.Description}"

aws logs filter-log-events --region {{ Inputs.region }} --log-group-name "{{ Inputs.log_group }}" --start-time {{ Tasks.time_window.output.data.start_ms }} --end-time {{ Tasks.time_window.output.data.end_ms }} --filter-pattern "{{ Inputs.log_filter }}" --max-items 50 --output json --query "events[].{Timestamp:timestamp,Stream:logStreamName,Message:message}"

params.script:
APP="${NB_APP:-}"
echo "===METRIC:failed_units==="
systemctl --failed --no-legend --plain 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '
echo "===METRIC:disk_max_pct==="
df -P -x tmpfs -x devtmpfs 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR>1 {gsub(/%/,"",$5); if ($5+0>m) m=$5+0} END {print m+0}'
echo "===METRIC:app_service_state==="
if [ -z "$APP" ]; then
  echo "not_checked"
elif [ -z "$(systemctl list-unit-files --no-legend "$APP.service" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
  echo "no_such_unit"
else
  systemctl is-active "$APP" 2>/dev/null | head -1
fi
echo "===SECTION:uptime_load==="
uptime 2>&1
echo "===SECTION:failed_units==="
systemctl --failed --no-pager 2>&1 | head -30
echo "===SECTION:app_service==="
if [ -n "$APP" ]; then systemctl status "$APP" --no-pager 2>&1 | head -30; else echo "no application name supplied"; fi
echo "===SECTION:disk==="
df -h -x tmpfs -x devtmpfs 2>&1
echo "===SECTION:memory==="
free -m 2>&1
echo "===SECTION:top_processes==="
ps -eo pcpu,pmem,pid,comm --sort=-pcpu 2>&1 | head -11
echo "===SECTION:listening_sockets==="
(ss -ltnp 2>/dev/null || netstat -ltnp 2>/dev/null) | head -30
echo "===SECTION:recent_errors==="
(journalctl -p err -n 100 --no-pager 2>/dev/null || tail -100 /var/log/messages 2>/dev/null || echo "no journal or syslog readable")
echo "===SECTION:app_journal==="
if [ -n "$APP" ]; then journalctl -u "$APP" -n 100 --no-pager 2>&1 || echo "no journal for unit $APP"; else echo "no application name supplied"; fi

ENDPOINTS="${NB_ENDPOINTS:-}"
echo "$ENDPOINTS" | tr ',' '\n' | while read -r ep; do
  ep=$(echo "$ep" | tr -d '[:space:]')
  [ -z "$ep" ] && continue
  host=${ep%:*}
  port=${ep##*:}
  if ! getent hosts "$host" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "$ep fail dns_resolution_failed"
    continue
  fi
  if timeout 5 bash -c "cat < /dev/null > /dev/tcp/$host/$port" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "$ep ok tcp_connect_succeeded"
  else
    echo "$ep fail tcp_connect_failed_or_timed_out"
  fi
done

evidences.title: Application diagnostic

definition.llm_description: Runs a deterministic first-level diagnostic for an application incident on AWS EC2 and returns a structured result (overall status, ranked findings, per-check coverage, raw evidence). Use it as the opening step of an EC2 or application incident — status check failures, an application that is down or degraded, unhealthy load balancer targets — to collect the instance, CloudWatch, load balancer, log, host and dependency evidence in one pass before deciding on a remediation runbook.
